nist_ai_rmf.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
nist_ai_rmf.version: AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1). NIST has said 1.0 is under revision.

eu_ai_act.name: EU AI Act
eu_ai_act.version: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)

controls.title: Accountable ownership
controls.requirement: A named executive owns enterprise AI risk. Every AI system and agent in the inventory has an accountable business owner and a technical owner, and their decision rights are written down.
controls.evidence: AI risk RACI; owner fields populated for every inventory entry.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: AI policy and risk appetite
controls.requirement: A board-approved AI policy sets risk appetite, prohibited uses and the highest autonomy tier the organisation will accept for each class of data and action. It is reviewed at least once a year and after any major AI incident.
controls.evidence: Approved policy with version history; board or committee minutes.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Regulatory obligations register
controls.requirement: The AI laws that apply to each system, and the dates they take effect, are recorded against that system, including its EU AI Act risk classification. The register is reviewed when the system or the law changes.
controls.evidence: Obligations register linked to the inventory; review log.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: AI literacy and role training
controls.requirement: People who build, approve, operate or oversee AI systems receive training for their role, including how prompt injection and agent misuse work. Completion is tracked.
controls.evidence: Training curriculum by role; completion records.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Governance of coding agents and SaaS-embedded AI
controls.requirement: AI capabilities embedded in SaaS platforms (such as office, CRM and ticketing copilots) and developer coding agents follow the same inventory, data-use and approval rules as custom-built agents. Vendor AI features default to off until reviewed, and coding agents operate with branch protection, mandatory human pull-request review and isolated credentials.
controls.evidence: SaaS AI feature review records; repository protection and coding-agent policy settings.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Inventory of AI systems, agents and components
controls.requirement: Every AI system, agent, model, MCP server and skill in use is recorded with its owner, purpose, data accessed, tools granted, autonomy tier and status. Discovery runs regularly to find unregistered use.
controls.evidence: Inventory export; discovery reports and how findings were resolved.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Autonomy and impact classification
controls.requirement: Each agent is assigned an autonomy tier based on what it can do without human approval, and an impact rating based on the worst credible outcome. Together they decide which controls apply.
controls.evidence: Classification record per system, approved by the risk owner.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Threat and impact assessment before release
controls.requirement: Systems at tier 2 and above, or rated high or severe impact, have a documented threat model and impact assessment, approved by the risk owner, before production and after any material change to tools, data or autonomy.
controls.evidence: Signed assessment; change records that triggered reassessment.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

controls.title: Safe retirement
controls.requirement: When an agent or component is withdrawn, its credentials are revoked, its memory and retrieval indexes are purged or archived under retention rules, its tool connections are removed and the inventory is updated.
controls.evidence: Decommissioning checklist; credential revocation records.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Approved sources for models, MCP servers and skills
controls.requirement: Models, MCP servers, skills and agent plugins are used only from an approved registry. New entries pass an intake review covering provenance, maintainer, licence, permissions requested, static scanning and adversarial testing.
controls.evidence: Registry with intake records; rejected-request log.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Version pinning and tool-definition change detection
controls.requirement: Approved components are pinned to a reviewed version or hash. Tool definitions are fingerprinted, and any change to a tool's description, schema or permissions blocks its use until it is reviewed again.
controls.evidence: Lock files or hashes; change alerts and their review outcomes.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Contract terms for AI providers
controls.requirement: Contracts with model and AI service providers cover data use and retention, training on customer data, incident notification, sub-processors, notice of model changes and audit rights.
controls.evidence: Contract clause checklist per provider.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Model version pinning and provider change management
controls.requirement: Production systems pin explicit model snapshots rather than rolling aliases where providers support it. Upstream model updates, deprecations or tool provider changes trigger regression testing before promotion, and high or severe impact systems maintain a documented fallback or exit path.
controls.evidence: Model version configuration; upgrade test records; exit plan for high and severe systems.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Distinct identity for every agent
controls.requirement: Each agent runs under its own non-human identity, never a shared account or a person's account, so every action can be traced to the agent and to the person or process that started it.
controls.evidence: Identity register; sample of actions traced end to end.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve

controls.title: Least privilege and short-lived delegated credentials
controls.requirement: Agents receive only the tools, scopes and data the task needs. Credentials are short-lived and bound to a specific task and resource; for MCP this means audience-bound tokens, and tokens are never passed through to downstream services.
controls.evidence: Scope reviews; token lifetime configuration; MCP authorization settings.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve

controls.title: Secrets kept out of agent context
controls.requirement: Credentials and keys never appear in prompts, agent configuration files, memory or tool descriptions. Agents obtain them from a secrets broker at the moment of use, and the model never sees them.
controls.evidence: Configuration scans; secrets-broker integration records.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: External content treated as untrusted
controls.requirement: Content from tools, documents, web pages, email and other agents is labelled as data, kept separate from instructions, and cannot on its own trigger a privileged action.
controls.evidence: Design review showing trust labelling; test results for indirect injection.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Scanning of agent instruction files
controls.requirement: Agent instruction files (skills, AGENTS.md, IDE rules, MCP configuration) are scanned in CI for hidden Unicode, override patterns and exfiltration sinks before they are merged or installed.
controls.evidence: CI configuration; scan results on recent merges.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Memory and retrieval integrity
controls.requirement: Writes to long-term memory and retrieval indexes are limited to trusted sources and tagged with their provenance. Memory can be inspected and purged per user and per agent.
controls.evidence: Write-path design; provenance fields; purge procedure and test.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve

controls.title: Hidden context and system-prompt protection
controls.requirement: System prompts, internal instructions and tool schemas are treated as extractable: they never hold secrets or serve as the sole access control, and applications are tested against prompt-extraction attacks before release.
controls.evidence: Prompt review confirming no secrets or sole controls; extraction test results.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Human approval for consequential actions
controls.requirement: Actions that move money, delete or change records, send external communications, change access or run code outside a sandbox need explicit human approval that shows the exact action and its parameters.
controls.evidence: Action catalogue with approval requirements; approval logs.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval

controls.title: Policy enforced outside the model
controls.requirement: Allowed tools, parameters, destinations and rates are enforced by a policy layer that the model cannot change. The model's own judgement is never the only control on what an agent does.
controls.evidence: Policy configuration; denied-action logs.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve

controls.title: Sandboxed code execution
controls.requirement: Code and commands generated by an agent run in an isolated, short-lived sandbox with no standing credentials and network access limited to an allow-list.
controls.evidence: Sandbox configuration; escape-test results.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval

controls.title: Egress and exfiltration controls
controls.requirement: Agents can reach only approved destinations. Outbound requests, rendered links and images are filtered so that data cannot leave through URLs or markdown.
controls.evidence: Egress allow-list; output-rendering filter tests.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Trust boundaries between agents
controls.requirement: Messages between agents are authenticated and treated as untrusted input. No agent can grant another more authority than it holds itself, and delegation depth and fan-out are capped.
controls.evidence: Inter-agent protocol design; authority-propagation tests.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval

controls.title: Resource and spend limits
controls.requirement: Each agent has limits on tokens, tool calls, spend and run time, and halts automatically when a limit is reached.
controls.evidence: Budget configuration; halt events.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Data classes approved per system and provider
controls.requirement: The classes of data each AI system and provider may process are defined. Restricted data cannot reach a model or tool that is not approved for it.
controls.evidence: Data-use matrix; DLP rules on AI traffic.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Safe handling of model output
controls.requirement: Model output is validated and encoded before it reaches browsers, shells, databases or other systems, in the same way as untrusted user input.
controls.evidence: Code review findings; output-handling tests.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or Moderate impact and above

controls.title: Permission-aware retrieval and tenant isolation
controls.requirement: Retrieval indexes, vector stores, semantic caches and agent memory enforce the invoking user's access permissions at query time and isolate data between tenants and roles so no query can surface unauthorised records.
controls.evidence: Retrieval authorisation design; cross-role and cross-tenant query test results.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or Moderate impact and above

controls.title: Privacy and secret minimisation in prompts and logs
controls.requirement: Personal data and secrets are redacted, tokenised or minimised before prompts reach external model providers and before prompts, parameters or results are written to operational logs, balancing auditability with privacy law.
controls.evidence: Redaction pipeline configuration; sample log inspection; retention and access controls.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Action-level logging
controls.requirement: Every prompt, tool call, parameter set, approval decision and result is logged with the agent's identity and a correlation ID, retained according to policy and protected from tampering.
controls.evidence: Log schema; retention settings; integrity controls.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Kill switch and credential revocation
controls.requirement: Any agent can be paused, its credentials revoked and its recent actions listed within a set time: 15 minutes for tier 3. The procedure is exercised at least twice a year.
controls.evidence: Runbook; exercise records with measured times.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or Severe impact

controls.title: AI incident response
controls.requirement: Incident runbooks cover prompt injection, data leakage through agents, runaway or rogue agents and compromised MCP servers, including regulatory notification where it is required. Staff and users have a clear channel to report concerns about an AI system's behaviour.
controls.evidence: Runbooks; exercise reports; incident records; reporting channel and its log.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Behavioural monitoring
controls.requirement: Each agent's normal behaviour is baselined. Unusual tools, destinations, volumes or deviation from the assigned goal raise an alert.
controls.evidence: Detection rules; alert history and triage outcomes.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

controls.title: Adversarial testing before release
controls.requirement: Systems at tier 2 and above, or rated high or severe impact, are tested before release, and after material change, for prompt injection, tool misuse and data leakage using a maintained attack corpus. Results are recorded against acceptance thresholds.
controls.evidence: Test reports with bypass rates against thresholds.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

controls.title: Continuous regression testing
controls.requirement: The attack corpus runs in CI against the production system prompt and configuration. A bypass rate above threshold blocks the release.
controls.evidence: CI pipeline; trend of bypass rate by release.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

controls.title: Independent assurance
controls.requirement: Tier 3 agents and severe-impact systems receive independent review, by internal audit or an external party, at least once a year.
controls.evidence: Assurance reports and management responses.
controls.applies_from: tier 3 Act autonomously, or Severe impact

controls.title: Accuracy, grounding and bias evaluation
controls.requirement: Systems are evaluated before release and after model or prompt changes for task accuracy, grounding against authoritative sources (hallucination rate) and, where outputs affect individuals or groups, bias and fairness across protected groups.
controls.evidence: Evaluation test sets, metrics, acceptance thresholds and sign-off records.
controls.applies_from: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

controls.title: Disclosure of AI interaction
controls.requirement: People are told when they are dealing with an AI system or receiving AI-generated content, and agents acting for someone identify themselves to third parties.
controls.evidence: UI copy; content-marking configuration; agent identification headers.
controls.applies_from: tier 0 Assist

controls.title: Oversight that is meaningful, not ceremonial
controls.requirement: Approval screens state what will happen and why, rather than asking for a bare yes or no. Approval rates and decision times are monitored to detect rubber-stamping.
controls.evidence: Approval UI review; approval-rate and decision-time metrics.
controls.applies_from: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

kris.name: Inventory coverage
kris.measure: Registered AI systems, agents and components with a named owner, as a share of all found by discovery

kris.name: Unregistered AI found
kris.measure: New AI tools, MCP servers or agents found in use without registration, per quarter

kris.name: Assessment currency
kris.measure: Tier 2 and 3 systems, and high or severe impact systems, whose threat and impact assessment reflects their current tools, data and tier

kris.name: Prompt injection bypass rate
kris.measure: Median share of the standard attack corpus that succeeds against tier 2 and 3 agents
kris.note: Use the same corpus every quarter so results are comparable, and add new techniques as a separate line until there is a baseline for them. Report the median across agents, and name any single agent above the red threshold. The [LLM Prompt Injection Fuzzer](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/llm-prompt-injection-fuzzer) produces this number per category.

kris.name: Time to stop an agent
kris.measure: Longest time, in the latest exercise, to pause a tier 3 agent and revoke its credentials
kris.red: > 60 min, or no exercise in 6 months
kris.note: Measure from the decision to stop until the agent has stopped acting and its credentials no longer work, not until someone has opened a ticket. An exercise that has not happened counts as red.

kris.name: Unreviewed tool changes
kris.measure: MCP tool definitions in use that changed since their last review
kris.note: MCP servers can change a tool's description after it has been approved. This indicator only works if tool definitions are fingerprinted at approval time; if they are not, report it as "not measurable" rather than zero.

kris.name: Rubber-stamp rate
kris.measure: Human approvals given in under three seconds, as a share of all approvals
kris.note: Three seconds is roughly the time it takes to read one line. A high rate usually means approvals are requested too often, not that reviewers are careless. The fix is fewer, clearer approval requests.

kris.name: Over-privileged agents
kris.measure: Agents holding scopes beyond their documented need at the last access review

kris.name: Agents without their own identity
kris.measure: Agents acting under a person's account or a shared account

kris.name: Overdue AI security findings
kris.measure: Critical and high findings on AI systems past their remediation deadline

kris.name: AI security incidents
kris.measure: Incidents involving AI systems in the quarter, by severity

kris.name: Training coverage
kris.measure: In-scope staff who completed role-based AI training in the last 12 months

kris.name: Overdue risk exceptions
kris.measure: Active AI policy or control exceptions past their 90-day expiry date (tracked in the [exception register](../templates/exception-register-template.md))

C1.name: User and approver
C1.why: Source of legitimate instructions, and the human check on consequential actions

C2.name: Orchestrator agent
C2.why: Decides what to do next; holds the agent's authority

C3.name: System prompt and instruction files
C3.why: Defines behaviour; includes skills, AGENTS.md, IDE rules and MCP configuration

C4.name: Tools and MCP servers
C4.why: Where the agent's actions take effect; tool descriptions and results are read by the model

C5.name: Memory and retrieval index
C5.why: Persists across sessions, so a poisoned entry keeps working

C6.name: Sub-agents and peer agents
C6.why: Can pass instructions and authority between agents

C7.name: Identity broker and secrets
C7.why: Issues the credentials the agent acts with

C9.name: Policy enforcement layer
C9.why: Enforces limits the model cannot change

threats.title: Direct prompt injection
threats.scenario: A user tells the agent to ignore its instructions and act outside its purpose.
threats.test: Injection corpus against the production prompt ([fuzzer](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/llm-prompt-injection-fuzzer))

threats.title: Indirect prompt injection
threats.scenario: A document, web page or email the agent reads contains instructions that redirect it.
threats.test: Indirect and tool-result probes ([fuzzer](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/llm-prompt-injection-fuzzer), [MCP harness](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/mcp-adversarial-harness))

threats.title: Tool poisoning
threats.scenario: An MCP server's tool description contains hidden instructions that the model follows whenever the tool is listed.
threats.test: Description-injection probes ([MCP harness](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/mcp-adversarial-harness))

threats.title: Tool rug pull
threats.scenario: A server behaves well during review, then changes its tool definitions or behaviour once approved.
threats.test: Fingerprint tool definitions at approval; alert on any difference ([MCP fingerprinting starter](../examples/mcp-fingerprint/README.md))

threats.title: Malicious instruction file
threats.scenario: A skill or rules file pulled from a marketplace or repository hides instructions in invisible Unicode or comments.
threats.test: Static scan in CI ([agentlint](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/agentlint))

threats.title: Exfiltration through a tool call
threats.scenario: Injected instructions make the agent send data to an attacker using a legitimate tool such as HTTP or email.
threats.test: Exfiltration probes ([MCP harness](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/mcp-adversarial-harness))

threats.title: Exfiltration through rendered output
threats.scenario: The agent outputs a markdown image or link whose URL carries conversation data; the client fetches it automatically.
threats.test: Image-exfiltration payloads; scan instruction files for image sinks ([agentlint](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/agentlint) rule AGT040)

threats.title: Destructive action
threats.scenario: The agent deletes data or changes configuration because of an injected or misunderstood instruction.
threats.test: Probes that request destructive tools; confirm approval gates hold

threats.title: Credential theft
threats.scenario: Keys or tokens placed in configuration, prompts or tool descriptions are read out by the model or harvested through a tool.
threats.test: Scan configuration for secrets and sensitive paths ([agentlint](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/agentlint) rule AGT042)

threats.title: Confused deputy
threats.scenario: A server acts with its own broad credentials on behalf of a user who should not have that access, or passes a user token through to another service.
threats.test: Confused-deputy probes ([MCP harness](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/mcp-adversarial-harness)); review token audience settings

threats.title: Memory poisoning
threats.scenario: An attacker gets an instruction written into long-term memory, where it influences later sessions and other users.
threats.test: Attempt memory writes from untrusted content; check provenance tags

threats.title: Retrieval index poisoning
threats.scenario: Planted documents in a retrieval index steer answers or carry indirect injections.
threats.test: Seed test documents; confirm they are excluded or labelled

threats.title: Sandbox escape
threats.scenario: Code written by the agent breaks out of its sandbox or reaches credentials and networks it should not.
threats.test: Escape and egress tests inside the sandbox

threats.title: Instructions spreading between agents
threats.scenario: A compromised agent passes injected instructions or excess authority to other agents, which act on them.
threats.test: Inject at one agent; trace whether others act on it

threats.title: Runaway consumption
threats.scenario: A loop or adversarial input makes the agent call tools or models without end, running up cost or exhausting a service.
threats.test: Load and loop tests against budgets

threats.title: Approval fatigue
threats.scenario: Approvals are requested so often, or presented so vaguely, that reviewers approve without reading.
threats.test: Measure approval time and rate; review approval screens

threats.title: Undetected goal drift
threats.scenario: The agent gradually pursues something other than its assigned goal, and no one notices.
threats.test: Compare actions against the agent's baseline and stated goal

threats.title: Cross-tenant or unauthorised retrieval
threats.scenario: The retrieval index or semantic cache returns documents belonging to another user, role or tenant because access controls are not enforced at query time.
threats.test: Query as a low-privilege or second-tenant user for restricted seed documents

threats.title: Hidden context and system-prompt extraction
threats.scenario: A user or injected prompt extracts the system prompt, internal tool instructions or business rules.
threats.test: Prompt-extraction probes ([fuzzer](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/llm-prompt-injection-fuzzer)); confirm no secrets or sole controls live in prompts

threats.title: Cross-server MCP tool shadowing
threats.scenario: A malicious or compromised MCP server registers a tool name or description that shadows or overrides a trusted server's tool across the same client session.
threats.test: Tool-shadowing probes ([MCP harness](https://github.com/thenayanhazra/mcp-adversarial-harness)); enforce namespaced tool allow-lists
